children: Meta Platforms'
new artificial intelligence shopping assistant is emerging as a potential threat to Amazon.com
, challenging the e-commerce giant's dominance over online shopping and its nearly $70 billion advertising business, The Wall Street Journal reported.
Meta

introduced Muse in September, allowing consumers to use AI agents to research products, make purchases and handle tasks such as travel bookings and budgeting. More than 10 million users in the United States and Canada created Muse agents during its first six weeks, according to Meta
For investors, the stakes extend beyond competition for retail sales. Amazon's

advertising business depends heavily on sponsored product placements that influence shoppers browsing its marketplace. AI agents that independently compare prices and select products could diminish the effectiveness of those advertisements, potentially undermining one of Amazon's most profitable revenue streams.
Amazon
has blocked Muse from making purchases on its platform, citing security concerns. Competitors including Walmart
and Shopify
have taken the opposite approach, establishing partnerships with Meta to accommodate AI-driven shopping.
Amazon

Chief Executive Andy Jassy downplayed the immediate threat during Thursday's earnings call, arguing that third-party shopping agents remain less convenient than purchasing directly from retailers. He said Amazon's
advertising business hasn't experienced a meaningful impact.
Jassy also highlighted Amazon's

own Alexa for Shopping, which helps consumers compare products, monitor prices and receive personalized recommendations. The assistant has attracted more than 400 million users over the past year, according to the company.
Nevertheless, industry observers warn that AI agents could weaken Amazon's

longstanding position as consumers' preferred starting point for online purchases. J.P. Morgan analysts see Muse as a potentially significant consumer AI platform, while venture capitalist Paul Graham has suggested Amazon's
restrictions could create opportunities for emerging competitors.
Amazon

is developing its own agent-driven commerce capabilities. Its Shop Direct service now features more than 250 million products from outside merchants, while Buy For Me enables customers to purchase certain third-party products without leaving Amazon's platform.
Amazon's

extensive fulfillment infrastructure, customer relationships and delivery capabilities could provide substantial competitive advantages even as shopping habits evolve. Analysts at Neuberger remain optimistic about the company's ability to adapt.
Jassy has also indicated that Amazon

could eventually collaborate with outside AI agents. Such partnerships could help preserve its retail dominance, although the company faces a difficult balancing act between accommodating new shopping technologies and protecting the advertising revenue generated by keeping consumers inside its ecosystem.
